string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the world\'s great ancient capitals, with over 3,000 years of history and more than 800 years as a national capital. Located in northern China, it is the country\'s political, cultural, educational, and international affairs centre, hosting the National People\'s Congress, the central government, and numerous top universities and research institutions. The city is famous for UNESCO World Heritage Sites including the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven, and the Summer Palace. It hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics. Beijing blends imperial landmarks and traditional hutong neighbourhoods with modern skyscrapers and a rapid transit network.

Shanghai is one of the world\'s largest cities and China\'s leading economic, financial, trade, and shipping centre. Situated on the east coast at the mouth of the Yangtze River, it began as a small fishing town and grew dramatically after opening as a treaty port in the mid-nineteenth century. The city is famous for its distinctive skyline, particularly the Bund\'s historic waterfront buildings and the futuristic skyscrapers of Pudong, including the Oriental Pearl Tower and Shanghai Tower. Shanghai is a global transport hub with one of the world\'s busiest container ports, and a major cultural destination featuring museums, theatres, and the historic Yu Garden. It hosted the 2010 World Expo.

Chongqing, formerly romanized as Chungking, is a large direct-administered municipality in southwest China, set at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. It became a direct-controlled municipality in 1997 to lead the development of the Three Gorges reservoir region. Built across steep hills and river valleys, the city is famous for its dramatic mountain terrain, dense clusters of high-rise buildings, and the elevated Liziba light-rail station that appears to pass through a residential tower. Chongqing is a major industrial and transport hub of western China, the starting point of Yangtze River cruises, and home to the UNESCO-listed Dazu Rock Carvings. It is also renowned for its fiery hotpot cuisine and the distinctive Hongyadong stilt-house complex.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, lying on the coast of the Bohai Sea around 120 kilometres southeast of Beijing. It serves as a major gateway port to the national capital and the surrounding industrial region. Opened as a treaty port in 1860, Tianjin developed a unique architectural heritage, and its former foreign concession districts display European-style villas and public buildings. The city is an important manufacturing, logistics, and marine-chemical base, while its cultural landmarks include the riverside Tianjin Eye Ferris wheel, the Ancient Culture Street, and the Five Great Avenues neighbourhood. Tianjin is also known for its distinctive folk culture, humour, and snack foods such as mahua fried dough twists.
